title: Nvidia Unveils First PCs Designed for AI Agents at Computex
summary: Nvidia announced its first personal computers purpose-built for AI agents at Computex, introducing the N1X processor and RTX Spark for consumer PCs alongside the Nemotron 3 Ultra model and the CUDA-X agent skills framework. The announcements extend Nvidia's AI dominance from data centres into edge devices, positioning the company to capture the emerging AI PC market as agentic workloads move closer to users.

title: Anthropic Confidentially Files for IPO at $965 Billion Valuation
summary: Anthropic filed a confidential S-1 with the SEC, setting the stage for what could be one of the largest technology IPOs in history. The company raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation, surpassing OpenAI's $852 billion round-valuation from March. Anthropic has told investors its annual revenue run rate will exceed $50 billion by end of July, with Q2 2026 revenue projected at $10.9 billion—more than double Q1's $4.8 billion. The filing potentially beats OpenAI to a public listing.

title: SoftBank to Invest €75 Billion in AI Data Centres Across France
summary: SoftBank announced plans to invest €75 billion to build AI data centres across France's Hauts-de-France region, targeting 5 gigawatts of compute capacity with Schneider Electric as an infrastructure partner. The commitment, announced at the Choose France summit hosted by President Macron, marks the largest single AI infrastructure pledge on the European continent and advances France's ambition to become a leading AI compute hub.

title: SpaceX Awarded $4.16 Billion U.S. Space Force Contract Under Golden Dome
summary: SpaceX has been awarded a $4.16 billion contract by the U.S. Space Force as part of the Golden Dome missile defence initiative. The contract cements SpaceX's position as the primary commercial partner for U.S. strategic space infrastructure and represents one of the largest single defence awards in the company's history.

title: Anthropic's Mythos Security Tool: Powerhouse or Budget Buster?
summary: Anthropic's internal AI security tool, Mythos, identified more than 25 vulnerabilities across partner systems within three weeks of deployment, according to a Palo Alto Networks assessment. The tool consumed more than one million tokens in operational use, raising questions about cost efficiency even as it demonstrates potent detection capabilities. The report highlights the dual challenge of deploying AI for cybersecurity at enterprise scale.

title: Anthropic Halves Approved List for Unofficial Share Trading
summary: Anthropic has cut in half the number of firms it recognizes as authorized venues for secondary trading of its shares, removing Hiive and other platforms from an informal approved list. The move tightens governance over pre-IPO liquidity as the company prepares for a public offering and signals Anthropic's intent to control its share price narrative ahead of its confidential SEC filing.

title: Meta Plans AI Pendant and Broader Wearables Line in Internal Memo
summary: An internal Meta memo authored by VP Alex Himel outlines plans for an AI pendant and an expanded wearables line, including a platform called Hatch for agentic AI and a Wearables for Work initiative. The memo signals Meta's intention to move well beyond smart glasses into a broader ecosystem of AI-embedded hardware, competing directly with Apple and emerging wearable AI startups.

title: Intel's Crescent Island Chip Targets Lower-Cost AI Inference
summary: Intel is preparing to launch Crescent Island, an AI inference chip designed to operate air-cooled with lower-cost memory, giving data centre operators a more affordable alternative to GPU-based inference clusters. The chip will be manufactured at Intel fabs and has undergone a China export-compliance assessment. The launch positions Intel to compete in the inference tier as customers push back on the cost of running large models at scale.

title: U.S. Closes AI Chip Export Loophole Used by Chinese Offshore Subsidiaries
summary: The Bureau of Industry and Security issued guidance on May 31 clarifying that Chinese companies routing AI chip purchases through offshore subsidiaries now require export licences, closing a loophole that had allowed restricted semiconductors to reach Chinese buyers via intermediaries. The move tightens the existing export control framework and is expected to affect a broad range of procurement structures previously used to circumvent the original restrictions.

title: China's MiniMax Releases M3 Open-Source Coding Model at a Fraction of Rival Costs
summary: MiniMax, the Hong Kong-listed AI company exploring a listing on Shanghai's Star market, released M3, an open-source model focused on AI coding tasks, priced at $0.12 per million tokens compared with approximately $5 for Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7. The release escalates competition in the open-source coding model segment and underscores the cost pressure Chinese AI labs are placing on Western frontier model providers.

title: Florida Attorney General Sues OpenAI Over ChatGPT's Role in FSU Shooting
summary: Florida filed a civil lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, becoming the first U.S. state to do so, alleging deceptive trade practices, negligence, and product liability failures. The suit centres on the April 2025 shooting at Florida State University, in which the alleged shooter reportedly used ChatGPT to plan the attack—querying the model on optimal campus locations and how many casualties would attract media attention. OpenAI denied responsibility, saying its responses drew on publicly available information.

title: The AI Trade Hits Overdrive as S&P 500 Posts Best Two-Month Run
summary: AI-related stocks have driven virtually all of the S&P 500's gains in recent months, with the index climbing roughly 15% since late March. AI infrastructure industries now represent more than half of the S&P 500 by market capitalization, and major tech companies have committed nearly $700 billion in capital expenditure for 2026. The rally has prompted debate over whether valuations have run ahead of near-term fundamentals.

title: Estonia Rolls Out ChatGPT Edu to All Secondary School Students Nationwide
summary: Estonia has become the first country to provide ChatGPT Edu licences to all secondary school students and teachers, covering approximately 20,000 students in grades 10 and 11 and 4,700 teachers in the initial rollout. The government's AI Leap program customizes the tool to act as a Socratic guide rather than a direct-answer engine, reflecting educator concerns about over-reliance on AI. Expansion to vocational schools covering an additional 38,000 students is planned for later in 2026.

title: Venture Capital Shifts Attention to Hardware Bets Beyond Language Models
summary: A growing cohort of VCs is backing hardware plays outside the large language model stack, including intelligence-layer chip architectures such as GraphOn and superconductor-based compute platforms. Investors argue that the compute bottleneck for the next wave of AI applications cannot be solved by scaling existing GPU designs, and that the hardware layer beneath LLMs represents an underinvested opportunity.

title: Kalshi and Coinbase Win CFTC Approval for Crypto Perpetuals in the U.S.
summary: Prediction market platform Kalshi and Coinbase have received CFTC approval to offer crypto perpetual futures contracts to U.S. retail customers, marking a significant expansion of leveraged crypto derivatives available to American investors. The approval follows a broader regulatory shift toward structured crypto products and could open a large new revenue stream for both platforms.

title: Blue Origin Rocket Explosion May Delay Amazon Kuiper and AST SpaceMobile Launches
summary: A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a hotfire test at Cape Canaveral, disrupting planned launch timelines for both Amazon's Project Kuiper satellite internet constellation and AST SpaceMobile's commercial broadband satellites. AST's commercial launch, previously scheduled for Q4 2026, is now expected to slip to Q1 2027. Amazon faces potential FCC deadline pressure and is expected to file for an extension on its obligation to have thousands of satellites in orbit.

title: Apple Smart Glasses Delayed to Late 2027 Amid Visual AI Concerns
summary: Apple has pushed back its first smart glasses (code-named N50) to late 2027 from an earlier target of early 2027, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. The delay stems from concerns that Apple's Visual Intelligence features are not yet robust enough to compete with Meta's Ray-Ban glasses in an established market. The glasses are expected to be priced between $200 and $500 and will feature oval cameras and multiple frame styles. A lighter Apple Vision Air headset is now expected no earlier than 2028.

title: Charter Communications Cyberattack Exposed Data of 4.9 Million Customers
summary: Charter Communications confirmed a cyberattack attributed to the ShinyHunters threat group that exposed personal data belonging to approximately 4.9 million customers. The breach is under investigation by federal authorities. ShinyHunters, known for previous high-profile data theft incidents, is believed to have exfiltrated customer records including names, addresses, and account information.

title: Qualcomm CEO Bets on Agentic AI at the Edge in Computex Keynote
summary: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon used his Computex keynote to position Qualcomm as the primary silicon enabler for agentic AI workloads running on-device, arguing that real-time, private, and low-latency AI agency requires processing at the edge rather than in the cloud. The pitch targets smartphone OEMs and PC makers as Qualcomm competes with Nvidia's agent-focused PC platform announcements at the same event.

title: e& Sells 12.5% Stake in Careem to Uber for $100 Million
summary: UAE telecoms group e& has sold a 12.5% stake in Careem, the Middle East ride-hailing and super-app platform, to Uber for $100 million, giving Uber an expanded foothold in the region. The deal deepens the commercial relationship between Uber and Careem, which Uber previously acquired before spinning out the super-app division to e&, and implicitly values the relevant Careem equity at approximately $800 million.

title: Saskatchewan Premier Says Provincial Social Media Bans for Minors Won't Work
summary: Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe expressed scepticism that province-level bans on social media access for minors would be effective, arguing that without a federal framework, teens can simply circumvent provincial restrictions. The comments come as Canadian provinces debate whether to follow emerging legislation in other jurisdictions that restricts social media access for those under 16 or 18.

title: Five Files to Follow This Week: Canadian Bank Earnings and Q1 GDP
summary: The Globe and Mail's weekly business brief highlights two major data releases: Canadian bank earnings reports and Statistics Canada's first-quarter GDP figures. Bay Street is watching for signs of credit quality deterioration and loan-loss provisioning given elevated interest rates, while the GDP print will indicate whether the Canadian economy maintained momentum through early 2026.
